newsitem.title: UK: UK'S Ashdown says lift EU debate out of sterility.
newsitem.headline: UK'S Ashdown says lift EU debate out of sterility.

text.p: Liberal Democrat leader Paddy Ashdown said the debate about the future of Europe should be lifted out of "its present sterility."
Writing in the London Times, he said the governance of the European Union is "wide, weak and loosely defined when it ought to be narrow, strong and sharply defined."
In a followup interview with BBC Radio, the centrist leader said he wanted his party to be "a rock on which you can depend in the process of sensible democratic integration of Europe".

"We have to lift the debate about Britain's future in Europe and the future of Europe, out of the sterility into which it has sunk when you are accused of being a Euro sceptic or proto Euro sceptic for suggesting ways Europe can work better."
Ashdown said a "politicians' Europe" had been created and he called for a "people's Europe" instead where European action was used to improve the lot of the citizens.
